input.summary:
parts/room-21.mjs furnishes the east upper corridor: a barrel-and-chest linen run and a dark-oak console with a potted plant and standing lantern on the north wall (z51), a red runner down the lane z52, and hanging lanterns down the lane and wing passage. Lanes kept clear for the hall door, master doors and wing opening.
Blocked: runParts refuses every write because shell.mjs:27 fills the whole house interior with air, which counts as owned, so the real build.nbt has 0 placed for this part.
Test build on the shell (lock bypassed) passes the fit (only "hallway to nowhere", because the hall is still a stub) and renders as intended; the box also overlaps the bedroom 5 and east bath boxes, which are still dark.
left: Blocked: the mansion shell fills the house interior with air (parts/shell.mjs:27 `fill(..., "air")`), and runParts counts every earlier-part write, air included, as owned. All 32 of this part's writes are refused (build.nbt has 0 placed for room 21). Fix belongs to the shell or to runParts: air the shell wrote into rooms should not lock those cells. Until then the part cannot land in the real build.
Not ticked in plan.md or elements.md: the part is not in build.nbt. The make.sh run did produce a whole build.nbt, but without this part.
Walk: the room reads UNREACHABLE only because the entrance hall and upper hall (room-1, room-13) are still stubs; the hall doorway at x51 z51..52 has no path in yet.

Light: the wing passage (x52..53 z53..60) and the corridor are lit 6-15 with the hanging lanterns at y16. Bedroom 5 (x55..60 z54..60) and the east bath (x63..68 z54..60) lie inside this room's box in rooms.json and are still dark (0-1) in the test build; their designers (room-22, room-23) must light them, or the box in rooms.json needs shrinking.
Chimney cells x61..62 z56..57 are left air for the roofs part; my furniture avoids them.

waste.what: Diagnosing why every write was refused: reading runParts' owned-set logic and the shell's air fill cell by cell, then dumping block ids on the floor row to see what was locked.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls, roughly 4 minutes of the 12
waste.tool: A `$MCD plan` / `mcd room` line that reports cells an earlier part set to air as locked, with the part name, so the lock cause shows up in one line of the make.sh output.

waste.what: Hand-indexed the 17-column floor rows for the furniture, one character per cell, to keep the lanes clear.
waste.cost: one sparse-map helper (rows({z: {x: char}})) written by hand in the module; no per-block set() calls
waste.tool: A `layers` variant that takes sparse {x,z: char} maps, plus a `$MCD plan --lanes` output that marks doorway first cells and lanes as no-go.

waste.what: Test-built onto the finished shell with a bypass script to get a room check and a render while the lock blocked the real build.
waste.cost: one throwaway script, one room check, one rooms render
waste.tool: A `mcd room --overlay <part.mjs>` option that runs a part onto the current build without runParts' lock, for checks only.

waste.what: Overlapping room boxes: rooms.json gives this room the bedroom 5 and east bath boxes, so the room check counts cells another designer owns.
waste.cost: found by reading the box and the dark-cell map; no tool flagged it
waste.tool: `mcd room` should warn when two rooms' boxes overlap, and `runParts` should report which earlier part owns each cell.

companions.task: Light bedroom 5 and the east bath, which sit inside this room's box, so the dark cells at z54..60 go away without my lanterns covering their rooms.
Change the shell's interior air fill (shell.mjs:27) so it no longer locks the rooms: air the shell wrote should be free for furnishers, or the rooms should be carved as box-free cells.
